# Tobit Chapter 13 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_013_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And Tobit wrote a prayer of rejoicing and said:

Blessed is the God who lives forever,
and blessed is his kingdom.

**2** For he chastises and he shows mercy;
he leads down to Hades and he leads up again,
and there is no one who can escape from his hand.

**3** Give thanks to him before the nations, O sons of Israel,
for he has scattered us among them.

**4** Declare his greatness there;
exalt him before every living creature,
for he is our Lord and our God,
he is our Father through all the ages.

**5** He will chastise us for our iniquities,
and yet again he will show mercy
and will gather us from all the nations
among whom you have been scattered.

**6** If you turn to him with your whole heart
and with your whole soul,
to do what is true before him,
then he will turn to you
and will not hide his face from you.
Look at what he has done for you;
give thanks to him with your whole mouth;
bless the Lord of righteousness
and exalt the King of the ages.
I give thanks to him in the land of my captivity,
and I declare his strength and his greatness
to a sinful nation.
Turn back, O sinners, and do righteousness before him;
who knows — perhaps he will look with favor on you
and show you mercy.

**7** I exalt my God;
my soul exalts the King of heaven
and rejoices in his greatness.

**8** Let all speak and give thanks to him in Jerusalem.

**9** O Jerusalem, the holy city,
he will chastise you for the deeds of your children,
and yet again he will have mercy on the children of the righteous.

**10** Give worthy thanks to the Lord,
and bless the King of the ages,
so that his tent may be rebuilt in you with joy,
and he may gladden in you those who are captive,
and may cherish in you those who are wretched,
through all generations forever.

**11** A bright light will shine to all the ends of the earth;
many nations will come to you from afar,
and the inhabitants of all the ends of the earth,
bearing in their hands gifts for the King of heaven.
Generations of generations will offer joyful worship in you,
and your name will be exalted forever,
age upon age.

**12** Cursed are all who speak a harsh word against you;
cursed are all who destroy you and tear down your walls,
all who overthrow your towers
and set fire to your dwellings;
but blessed forever are all who revere you.

**13** Go then and rejoice over the children of the righteous,
for all will be gathered together
and will bless the Lord of the ages.

**14** Blessed are those who love you,
and blessed are those who will rejoice
over your peace.
Blessed are all the people
who will grieve over you
because of all your afflictions,
for they will rejoice in you
when they see all your glory,
and they will be glad forever.

**15** My soul, bless the Lord, the great King.

**16** For Jerusalem will be built with sapphires
and emeralds and precious stone;
your walls and your towers and your battlements
with pure gold;
and the streets of Jerusalem
with beryl and ruby and stone of Ophir
will be paved.

**17** And the gates of Jerusalem will be built
with sapphire stones and gems,
and all her lanes will cry out "Hallelujah"
and sing "Praise the Lord,"
as they celebrate in her —
blessed forever and ever.

**18** My soul, bless the Lord, the great King.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

Chapter 13 is the only sustained poetic/liturgical passage in Tobit. I have rendered it in free verse, maintaining line breaks that reflect the structural parallelism of the Greek. The chapter has clear strophic organization: theophanic declaration (vv. 1–2), exile lament (vv. 3–6), personal doxology (vv. 7–8), address to Jerusalem (vv. 9–14), and the gemstone vision (vv. 15–17), with a doxological frame (v. 18).

The divine titles are consistent throughout: "King of the ages" (*basileus tōn aiōnōn*), "King of heaven" (*basileus tou ouranou*), "Lord of righteousness" (*kyrios tēs dikaiosynēs*). These are rendered formally without paraphrase.

The gemstone list in vv. 16–17 draws on Isaiah 54:11–12 and prefigures Revelation 21. I render each stone as its established English name: sapphire, emerald, beryl, ruby. "Stone of Ophir" is kept as a proper compound.

Verse 6 is structurally dense. I break the conditional clause ("If you turn...") clearly from the divine response clause ("then he will turn...") and the autobiographical section ("I give thanks...") to preserve the logical structure.

— LOGOS
